paragraphs.source_en: After offering his congratulations on the victory at the camps on Chausuyama and Okayama, Katagiri Katsumoto returned to his own tent near the Black Gate. He had a folding stool carried outside, sat there without stirring, and stared fixedly at the charred main enclosure of Osaka Castle. His face was gaunt, his hair dishevelled, and he looked as wild as a demon. This was not the fatigue of days of battle, but the anguish born of spending every waking hour searching for a way to preserve the Toyotomi clan.
